skill.name: analyzing-docs

skill.summary: Evaluate codebase documentation and produce prioritized, measurable recommendations.

content.value_statement: Incomplete documentation makes code harder to use, maintain, and review. This skill measures coverage and quality, identifies gaps, and prioritizes improvements.
actual_capabilities: Measures documentation coverage for functions, classes, modules, files, and projects.
Scores completeness, accuracy, clarity, and usefulness on a defined scale.
Identifies undocumented public APIs, missing examples, outdated content, and absent error details.
Provides language-specific grep patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go.
Produces a structured report with metrics, critical gaps, and prioritized recommendations.
limitations: Coverage calculations depend on accurate counts of documentable and documented items.
Quality scores require judgment and may vary between reviewers.
The included search patterns cover only JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go.
The skill analyzes documentation but does not create or update missing documentation.

use_cases.title: Assess Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Review public API documentation before a release and identify critical omissions.

use_cases.title: Plan Documentation Work
use_cases.description: Measure documentation gaps and create a prioritized improvement backlog.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Repository Health
use_cases.description: Compare documentation coverage and quality across modules or repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Documentation Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the documentation in [path]. List the most important gaps and explain their impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused review of one directory or component.

prompt_templates.title: Measure Documentation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [repository] and calculate documentation coverage for functions, classes, modules, and project guides. Show counts and percentages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when baseline coverage metrics are needed.

prompt_templates.title: Score Documentation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess documentation in [path] for completeness, accuracy, clarity, and usefulness. Score each dimension from 0 to 10 with evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a detailed quality assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Prioritized Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository] documentation. Measure coverage, score quality, identify critical gaps, compare modules, and recommend prioritized actions with measurable targets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a comprehensive repository improvement plan.

output_examples.input: Assess documentation coverage for the public API.
output_examples.output: Overall coverage: 72%. Public classes are well documented, but exported functions lack parameter details. Prioritize authentication and error-handling APIs.

output_examples.input: Score the quality of the developer guide.
output: Completeness: 7/10. Setup and deployment are covered, but troubleshooting is missing.
Accuracy: 8/10. Commands match the current project configuration.
Clarity: 6/10. Several sections use undefined terms.
Usefulness: 7/10. Add failure examples and recovery steps.

output_examples.input: Identify the most urgent documentation gaps.
output_examples.output: Critical gaps: undocumented public methods, missing security warnings, and outdated request examples. Address public API contracts before formatting inconsistencies.

best_practices: Define the repository scope and documentation audience before analysis.
Validate documentation claims against current code and runnable examples.
Support every score with file-specific evidence and prioritized recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat comment counts as proof of useful documentation.
Do not average scores without explaining critical omissions.
Do not recommend broad rewrites when focused updates can close measured gaps.

faq.question: What documentation does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates functions, classes, modules, file-level notes, README files, API references, architecture documents, and onboarding guides.

faq.question: How is documentation coverage calculated?
faq.answer: Coverage is the number of documented items divided by the total documentable items, multiplied by 100.

faq.question: Which quality dimensions are scored?
faq.answer: The framework scores completeness, accuracy, clarity, and usefulness from 0 to 10.

faq.question: Does the skill modify documentation files?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes existing documentation and recommends changes, but it does not write or update files.

faq.question: Which programming languages have included search patterns?
faq.answer: The skill includes example search patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go.

faq.question: Can the scores compare repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the same scope, counting rules, and scoring criteria for each repository to make comparisons meaningful.
